synopses.short: Highlights of Amy's BBC performances introduced by Jools Holland in a programme from 2011.
synopses.medium: Jools Holland introduces a selection of Amy's BBC session performances, including her first appearance on Janice Long's Radio 2 show in September 2003. First broadcast in 2011.
synopses.long:
Throughout her recording career Amy Winehouse made regular appearances on BBC Radio. 

Starting with her first live session on Janice Long's Radio 2 show in September 2003, Jools Holland traces Amy's BBC session performances on programmes including Radio 1's Live Lounge and Radio 2's Dermot O' Leary and Drivetime shows. With appearances from Janice Long, Jo Whiley, Clare Teal, Chris Evans, Dermot O' Leary and Gilles Peterson. 

First broadcast in 2011 and repeated as part of an Artist Collection marking the 10th anniversary of Amy Winehouse's tragic death at the age of 27.

titles.display_title: Jo Whiley - Amy Winehouse - Legacy of a Lioness, Episode 2

synopses.short: Emeli Sandé and Mabel celebrate Amy Winehouse's life and legacy.
synopses.medium: In a programme first broadcast 10 years after her death, Emeli Sandé and Mabel celebrate Amy's life and legacy. They share their favourite Amy songs and discuss how she inspired them.
synopses.long: Originally broadcast in 2021 to mark 10 years since the tragic passing of singer and artist, Amy Winehouse, one of the UK’s greatest music talents. Her story has been well told over the years, but now looking back, her legacy lives on. Amy led the way as a British female voice in reaching a worldwide audience. Although hugely talented in their own right, many of today's biggest artists recognise this contribution to their own careers, including multi-award-winning singer-songwriter Adele. In this two-part special, UK female artists Jessie Ware, Emeli Sandé, Mabel, Ella Henderson and Alexandra Burke share their favourite songs and memories of Amy and discuss how she inspired them in their careers. In episode two we’ll continue to celebrate Amy’s life and legacy, taking a trip down memory lane playing songs from Amy's short but explosive career, and we’ll hear from female artists Emeli Sandé and Mabel - sharing their personal connections to Amy, and discussing some of the things that made her so unique from her distinctive tone to her iconic style.

synopses.short: Matt Everitt profiles each of the 12 shortlisted albums.
synopses.medium: Matt Everitt profiles each of the 12 shortlisted albums.
synopses.long:
In the run-up to BBC Radio 6 Music’s live coverage of the 2026 Mercury Prize Award Show, which takes place on Thursday 22 October at Newcastle’s Utilita Arena, Matt Everitt presents 2026 Mercury Prize, Pocket Guides.

Across three episodes (Monday 19th, Tuesday 20th and Wednesday 21st October, 11pm-12am), Matt will profile each of the 12 shortlisted albums – four per episode. The programmes will feature archive interviews and more.

Tonight's episode dives into A Great Day In Newcastle by Knats, Don't Look Down by Kojey Radical, Emotional Junglist by Nia Archives and The Art of Loving by and Olivia Dean. There's also a new interview with Nia Archives about what it means to be nominated for a Mercury Prize.

Monday's episode explored The Boy Who Played the Harp by Dave, Blizzard by Dove Ellis, Everybody Scream by Florence + The Machine and THAT’S SHOWBIZ BABY! by JADE.

Wednesday’s episode features The Boys of Dungeon Lane by Paul McCartney, THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE. by RAYE, Antidepressants by Suede and War Child Records’ HELP(2).
